purpose: Test on independent UTC windows whether the large H10S2-versus-H10N1 10-80 Hz baseline-power difference observed post-run in the failed T-phase positive control replicates outside all event/noise windows used by that control.

frequency_contract.selection_basis: Exactly the same fixed interior passband used by the already-completed in-band positive control; no frequency retuning is permitted.

independent_window_contract.selection_rule: Exactly one 10-minute window beginning 12:00:00 UTC on each listed date, on both stations. Dates were frozen before any of these independent windows were downloaded by this gate.

per_window: raw 10-80 Hz integrated power for H10N1 and H10S2
response-corrected 10-80 Hz integrated power for H10N1 and H10S2
S2-minus-N1 raw power ratio in dB
S2-minus-N1 corrected power ratio in dB
aggregate: median raw power per station over all complete paired windows
median corrected power per station over all complete paired windows
median of per-window S2-minus-N1 raw dB ratios
median of per-window S2-minus-N1 corrected dB ratios

replication_threshold.engineering_interpretation: 6 dB is approximately a fourfold power difference and is fixed here as a large station-baseline asymmetry effect size before these independent windows are downloaded.
replication_threshold.required: Both median per-window raw S2-minus-N1 dB and median per-window corrected S2-minus-N1 dB must be >= 6 dB, with at least 15 complete paired windows.

claim_ceiling: A replicated asymmetry establishes only that H10S2 has a substantially higher 10-80 Hz baseline power than H10N1 across this independent frozen time sample. It does not identify the physical cause, prove sensor malfunction, validate or invalidate any 119-Hz target claim, or convert the failed cross-station positive control to PASS. A non-replication likewise does not erase the completed control result.
